title: Mayor's Statement on tragic incident at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, AB
content: Today, Council, staff and residents of the City of Kitchener join a mourning nation following the tragic events of October 17 at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta.

On behalf of our entire community, I offer our deepest condolences to the families, loved ones and colleagues of all who lost their lives during yesterday’s tragic incident in a training area at CFB Wainwright.

We also send our wishes for healing to all those who were injured during yesterday’s incident - one of the worst tragedies for the Forces on Canadian soil in peacetime. May they find strength in the love and support of family, friends and a caring nation.

We extend our thoughts and prayers to all members of the Canadian Armed Forces, the broader military community and the community of Wainwright as they navigate this profound loss. We are deeply grateful to the first responders, medical teams, municipal staff and others who responded with urgency and care in Wainwright, Edmonton and elsewhere to support those affected.

This tragedy is a reminder of the risks and sacrifices the brave men and women of the Canadian Forces make in training and in service to our country. Our community stands in gratitude with all those who serve and those who have served.

To those in our community who serve in the Canadian Forces, full-time, reservists or veterans - please do not hesitate to reach out for support as you cope with the extent of this tragedy. To those in the community who know someone in the military or want to help, please consider checking in on those you know or making a blood donation through Canadian Blood Services .
In honour of those we lost, flags at Kitchener City Hall and all municipal facilities have been lowered to half-mast until further notice.
Today, and every day, we think of those who serve in our community and across the country. Kitchener stands in solidarity and sorrow with you at this difficult time.
Berry Vrbanovic
Mayor, City of Kitchener

title: Kitchener Fire Department Major Incident Update:  Activa Ave
content: On October 16, at 8:23 p.m., Kitchener Fire crews responded to a significant structure fire involving an eight-unit residential townhouse block on Activa Avenue. Flames and smoke were visible from the roof above four units when crews arrived.
Four units sustained fire, smoke, and water damage, and the occupants will not be permitted to return to those units at this time. Damage is currently estimated between $500,000 and $750,000.

Primary and secondary searches of all units were completed, and it was confirmed that everyone had safely evacuated the building. There were no reported injuries to civilians or firefighters, and the fire is not considered suspicious at this time.
Working smoke alarms were observed on all levels of every unit.
The Ontaio Fire Marshal was notified, and Kitchener Fire's investigation team will attend today to begin determining the cause of the fire.

title: Kitchener Fire Department: Major incident report – October 16, 2026
content: On Friday, October 16, at 8:23 p.m., Kitchener Fire crews responded to a significant structure fire involving an eight-unit residential townhouse block on Activa Avenue. Upon arrival, crews encountered a fire affecting four units and extended into the attic spaces.

A primary search of the building has been completed. Fire crews will remain on scene to monitor for hot spots, conduct overhaul operations, and secure the property. The Ontario Fire Marshal will be notified, and Kitchener Fire's investigation team will attend in the morning to begin determining the cause of the fire.

Residents of the affected units will be displaced, and hydro meters are being removed as a precaution. Damage is currently estimated between $500,000 and $750,000. There is structural roof damage to the four affected units.
There were no reported injuries to civilians or firefighters, and the fire is not considered suspicious at this time.

title: Community excitement inspires week-long grand opening celebration to mark the opening of Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park, November 14 to 22
content: What started as a one-day event has grown into a nine-day community celebration, as excitement continues to build around the opening of Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park.

From November 14 to 22, residents of all ages are invited to explore Kitchener's newest recreation destination at their own pace – and at no charge. Visitors can pre-register to take part in activities, try new programs and facility amenities and watch local athletes play.

The expanded celebration will give residents more time to discover everything the new facility has to offer, from aquatics and fitness to community recreation, sport experiences and family activities. The now week-long free event is designed to inspire residents to connect with their neighbours, try new programming, meet City staff and community sport organizations, and experience the spaces that will serve their community for generations to come.

"We heard Kitchener residents loud and clear: one opening day simply wasn't enough," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "The enthusiasm for the Grand Opening has been remarkable. By extending the celebration across nine days, we're creating more opportunities for residents of all ages to experience this incredible community space and discover the programs, services and connections that will make Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park such an important part of Kitchener's future."
Nine days. Countless ways to connect, compete, and belong.
The celebration will unfold over nine days, across three distinct experiences. Pre-register beginning on November 2 for free programming such as public swims.

Official ribbon-cutting ceremony | November 14 |10 a.m.11:30 a.m. Residents are invited to join Mayor Berry Vrbanovic, members of Kitchener City Council and community partners for the official ribbon-cutting ceremony celebrating the grand opening of the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park. The ceremony will mark the beginning of a new chapter for recreation, sport and community connection in Kitchener, followed by opportunities to explore the facility and take part in fun, family-friendly activities. Community members of all ages are encouraged to attend and help celebrate this exciting milestone for the City.

Celebrate and play | November 14 | Community activities: 12- 6 p.m.; Free registered programming: 7-10 p.m.  The festivities kick-off at noon on Saturday November 14 with a community celebration, featuring family-friendly entertainment, inflatables, face painting, mascots, information booths from local sport organizations and community groups, recreation experiences, public swims and opportunities to explore the facility.

Try Cowan Recreation Centre | November 15 to 20 | All day Starting on Sunday, November 15, and continuing throughout the week, residents can experience the facility firsthand through free recreational programming designed to meet a range of skills and abilities, including fitness and wellness classes, aquatics programs, recreation sports, active aging opportunities, youth activities and facility tours. Pre-registration through ActiveNet is required for most activities. Drop-in activities will be available on Sunday, November 15.

Discover local sport | November 21 and 22 | All day The celebration concludes with a showcase of local sport organizations, giving residents an opportunity to watch demonstrations, meet local community partners and discover pathways to lifelong participation in sport, recreation and active living.

Plan your visit Visitors are encouraged to consider carpooling or taking transit and allow extra time to arrive. Parking at Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park will be limited throughout the celebration, and some activities and programs require advance registration.

While the grand opening marks the beginning of a new chapter, the real story will be written by the residents who walk through these doors in the years ahead. The City of Kitchener looks forward to welcoming the community to Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park and celebrating the role it will play in a community that moves you.
To stay up to date on grand opening details, registration and more, visit Kitchener.ca/RBJSchlegelPark.
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener media@kitchener.ca

title: Strong start to advance voting in Kitchener's 2026 municipal election
content: Voter turnout during the first three days of advance voting for Kitchener's 2026 municipal election has exceeded turnout recorded during the first three days of advance voting in the 2022 election, demonstrating strong early participation from residents.

A total of 5,347 voters cast ballots during the first three days of advance voting in 2026, compared to 3,973 voters during the same period in 2022, representing an increase of approximately 35 per cent . These figures do not include home visits, institutional voting, or special voting locations.

"We're encouraged to see such strong turnout in the first days of advance voting," said Amanda Fusco, City Clerk. "The decisions made by municipal government have a direct impact on residents' daily lives, from the roads and trails they use, to recreation programs, housing, public spaces and essential services. Every vote is an opportunity to help shape the future of our community, and we encourage all eligible voters to participate."

Turnout has exceeded 2022 levels on each of the first three advance voting days. More than 1,700 eligible voters participated on each day of advance voting so far, with the highest single-day turnout occurring on October 15 when 1,827 ballots were cast.

Voting activity has been strong across the City. Stanley Park Community Centre recorded the highest turnout during the first three days of advance voting with 1,408 voters, followed by Forest Heights Community Centre with 1,228 voters. Country Hills Community Centre, Doon Pioneer Park Community Centre, Breithaupt Centre and Kitchener City Hall have also seen steady voter participation.
Residents who have not yet voted still have several opportunities to cast a ballot before Election Day.
Advance voting
Friday, October 16, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.
Saturday, October 17
Election Day voting
Election Day is Monday, October 26, 2026. Voting locations across the City will be open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Voters may vote at any voting location within their ward.
Additional voting options

The City also offers accessible voting supports, curbside voting, proxy voting and home vote upon request for eligible voters. Voting opportunities are also available for residents of participating retirement homes and long-term care facilities.
The City encourages all eligible voters to make a plan to vote, confirm their voter information and review available voting options before heading to the polls.
For information about voter registration, voting locations, accessibility supports and voting options, visit KitchenerVotes.ca.

title: City of Kitchener investment supports local innovation and enhances customer experience at Cowan Recreation Centre
content: The City of Kitchener is investing in local innovation and supporting local jobs through the purchase of a robotic floor cleaner from Kitchener-based company Avidbots . Developed and manufactured in Kitchener, the new robotic floor cleaner will be used to maintain the 33,800 square foot quad-gymnasium floor at the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park, set to open late this year.

This investment reflects the City's commitment to supporting local businesses and strengthening Kitchener's economy while continuing to provide high-quality services and experiences for residents at its community facilities.

"Kitchener is home to innovative companies that are developing world-class technology and creating meaningful local jobs," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "When opportunities exist to support local businesses while meeting operational needs, it creates benefits that extend well beyond a single purchase. At this critical time for Canada, investments like this one in Avidbots demonstrates how municipalities like Kitchener can support local and build Canada’s and Kitchener’s economic development, innovation and local employment opportunities, while also continuing to deliver excellent service to residents."

The robotic cleaner uses advanced sensors and autonomous navigation technology to efficiently clean large indoor spaces while maintaining consistent cleaning standards. The technology will help ensure the space is clean, safe and ready for residents participating in sports, fitness programs, community events and drop-in activities.

"As a company founded in Kitchener, we're thrilled to see Avidbots technology supporting the City at the new Cowan Recreation Centre," said JJ Ethridge, CEO of Avidbots. "We're proud to help create cleaner, safer, and more welcoming spaces for residents and visitors, while showcasing robotics innovation born and built in our community."
About Avidbots

Avidbots is a Kitchener-based robotics company specializing in autonomous cleaning solutions for commercial, industrial and public facilities. Its innovative technologies are used by organizations across North America and around the world to enhance cleaning efficiency and operational performance.
About RBJ Schlegel Park, home of Cowan Recreation Centre

RBJ Schlegel Park is where sport, recreation, and community come together. As Waterloo Region's premier destination for year-round activity, the park brings together indoor and outdoor spaces where residents of all ages and abilities can connect, compete, and belong.

The Cowan Recreation Centre will welcome more than 500,000 visits annually and support over 30 local sport organizations. Featuring two pools, a FIFA-sized field house, quad gymnasium, indoor walking track, indoor cricket nets, and flexible community spaces, the facility will increase programming opportunities and support recreation, wellness, tournaments, events, and community connection for generations to come. For updates and more information, visit Kitchener.ca/CRC .

title: Buy Canada–Buy Ontario events connect local businesses with government opportunities
content: Kitchener businesses gain practical information, new contacts and a clearer path to competing for public-sector work

Local construction companies and businesses from a range of sectors connected directly with federal and provincial procurement experts today during two Buy Canada–Buy Ontario events at Kitchener City Hall.

Hosted by the City of Kitchener, Mayor Berry Vrbanovic and Senator Sandra Pupatello, the events brought representatives from Supply Ontario, Public Services and Procurement Canada and Infrastructure Ontario together to help businesses better understand how to find government opportunities, register as suppliers and prepare to compete for public-sector contracts.
These are part of Kitchener’s Plan to Support Local and Protect Jobs , which includes practical actions to strengthen local businesses, open doors to new markets and help protect local jobs.

“Local businesses have the skills, experience and expertise governments need, but they also need clear information about where opportunities are posted, what buyers are looking for and how to compete,” said Kitchener Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “By bringing federal and provincial procurement experts directly to Kitchener, thanks to the support of Senator Sandra Pupatello, we are helping businesses make new connections, reach new customers and take practical steps toward winning new work. When local companies grow, they support local workers, strengthen our economy and build greater confidence to invest in Kitchener.”
Focused support for construction businesses
The morning, moderated by Jeff MacIntyre, President of the Grand Valley Construction Association, focused on construction and infrastructure companies.
Businesses learned:
Helping businesses across all sectors reach new customers

The afternoon, moderated by Ian McLean, President of the Greater Kitchener Waterloo Chamber of Commerce, was open to businesses of all sizes and sectors. It focused on helping companies understand whether government could become a customer for their products or services and what they need to do to get started.
Businesses learned:
The discussion also covered the wide range of goods and services governments purchase, from equipment and technology to professional services and everyday operational supplies.

“Businesses outside capital regions may not always be aware of the opportunities available to provide goods and services to government,” said Senator Sandra Pupatello. “Whether in construction or other sectors, Kitchener-Waterloo companies should be well positioned to take advantage of these new government policies.”

Participants left today with government procurement resources and a clearer understanding of the steps they can take to pursue public infrastructure work. This includes reviewing opportunities through CanadaBuys, exploring provincial opportunities through Supply Ontario and following up with the contacts made.

These events build on the City’s work to connect Kitchener businesses with new customers and markets. By improving access to procurement information and bringing the people who understand these systems directly into the community, the City is helping local businesses make informed decisions about future growth.
When Kitchener companies reach new customers and win new work, they support local jobs, keep expertise in the community and build a stronger, more resilient local economy.
For more information about the City’s work to support local businesses, visit Kitchener.ca/SupportLocal .
